mechanism_narrative: Accelerating GDP growth, measured by the year-over-year change in real GDP, signals a strengthening economy that will boost corporate earnings and drive positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Yield curve inverts (10y-2y < 0) within the next 6 months, indicating a looming recession that will negate the positive earnings signal from accelerating GDP.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in industrial production, measured by the year-over-year change in the INDPRO index, signals a supply shock that will negatively impact S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX posts positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances following a sharp INDPRO drop, indicating the market is shrugging off the supply shock.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid rise in the unemployment rate, measured by the 3-month change in UNRATE, signals a weakening labor market that will negatively impact consumer spending and drive negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Consumer confidence (Conference Board index) rises by > 5 points within the next 3 months, indicating the labor market deterioration is temporary and not impacting spending.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid rise in the federal funds rate, measured by the 3-month change in FEDFUNDS, signals a tightening monetary policy that will negatively impact S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX posts positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances following a rapid FEDFUNDS rise, indicating the market is shrugging off the tightening signal.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in housing starts, measured by the month-over-month change in HOUST, signals a weakening housing market that will negatively impact S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Building materials and homebuilder stocks (XHB, ITB) outperform SPX by > 2% over the next 20 trading days, indicating the housing market drop is not impacting broader demand.

mechanism_narrative: An accelerating pace of job growth, measured by the 3-month change in PAYEMS, signals a strengthening labor market that will boost consumer spending and drive positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Retail sales (RSX) and consumer discretionary stocks (XLY) underperform SPX by > 2% over the next 60 trading days, indicating the job growth is not translating into consumer spending.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid rise in consumer prices, measured by the 3-month change in CPIAUCSL, signals an inflation scare that will negatively impact S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: TIPS (TIP) and gold (GLD) underperform nominal bonds (TLT) by > 2% over the next 20 trading days, indicating the inflation scare is fleeting and not impacting real yields.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in the M2 money supply, measured by the 3-month change in RSAFS, signals a liquidity crunch that will negatively impact S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: High-yield bonds (JNK) and leveraged loans (BKLN) outperform investment-grade bonds (LQD) by > 2% over the next 20 trading days, indicating the liquidity crunch is not impacting credit markets.
